# Olist E-Commerce Analytics: Insights Report

*Generated by `python/run_all.py` from 99,441 orders placed between 2016-09-04 and 2018-10-17.
Trend figures use complete months only (2017-01 to 2018-08).*

## 1. Business snapshot
| KPI | Value |
|---|---|
| Valid orders (excl. canceled/unavailable) | 98,207 |
| Unique customers | 94,990 |
| GMV (price + freight) | R$ 15.74M |
| Product revenue | R$ 13.49M |
| Average order value | R$ 160.24 |
| Average review score | 4.12 / 5 |
| Late-delivery rate | 6.8% |
| Repeat-customer rate | 3.04% |

## 2. Key findings

**Growth.** Jan-Aug 2018 GMV was 140.4% higher than Jan-Aug 2017
(orders 137.3% higher). The single biggest month was 2017-11
(7,423 orders vs a median month of 5,084).

**Retention is the biggest problem.** Only 3.04% of customers ever placed a
second order, and they generate 5.66% of GMV. On average only
0.46% of a month's new customers buy again the following month
(across 20 cohorts). Growth depends almost entirely on new-customer acquisition.

**Late delivery damages satisfaction, and the effect is statistically significant.**
6.8% of delivered orders arrived after the promised date. Late orders average
2.27 stars vs 4.29 for on-time orders, and
62.4% of late orders get a 1-2 star review vs 9.3% on time
(relative risk 6.74x). Mann-Whitney U p < 0.001;
chi-square p < 0.001; 95% CI for the drop in mean score:
1.98 to 2.06 stars.

**Promises are padded.** Orders take 12.6 days on average against a promised
23.7 days. The worst state for lateness is Alagoas
(21.4% late); the best is Parana
(4.0%).

**Revenue is concentrated.** 18 of 74 categories
make 80% of product revenue; the top 3 (Health Beauty, Watches Gifts, Bed Bath Table) make
25.9%. Sao Paulo alone is 37.4% of GMV, and
the top 3 states are 62.5%.

**Freight is a hidden price.** Freight adds 16.6% on top of product
price overall, and 29.7% in Food Drink.

**Payments.** Credit card is the main method for 75.5% of orders
(boleto 19.9%); 68.0% of card orders use instalments.

**When people buy.** The busiest weekday is Mon, the quietest Sat;
81.6% of orders are placed between 10:00 and 22:59.

**RFM.** Champions are 1.1% of customers but
2.4% of GMV. "At Risk High-Value" customers (14.7%
of customers, average spend R$ 309.11) are the best win-back target.

## 3. Recommendations
1. **Launch a second-purchase programme.** Send a post-delivery voucher and category-based
   recommendations to first-time buyers. Even moving the repeat rate from
   3.04% up by a few points adds revenue without acquisition cost.
2. **Fix delivery promises first in the worst states.** Set state-specific estimated dates and
   carrier SLAs, starting with Alagoas. Lateness is the main
   measurable driver of 1-2 star reviews.
3. **Seller quality programme.** Track the seller scorecard (`sql/06`). Warn or coach sellers with
   an average review below 3.5 or more than 15% late deliveries.
4. **Win back "At Risk High-Value" customers** with targeted offers in their past categories.
5. **Freight-aware pricing.** Test free-shipping thresholds in high-freight categories,
   where shipping cost is a large share of the basket.

## 4. Data quality notes
| Issue found in raw data | Rows | Handling |
|---|---:|---|
| Orders with multiple reviews | 551 | kept the latest review per order |
| Products without a category | 610 | labelled "Unknown" |
| Payments 'not_defined' / zero value | 9 | removed |
| Delivered status but no delivery date | 8 | excluded from delivery metrics |
| Delivery date before purchase date | 0 | excluded from delivery metrics |
| Orders without items | 775 | kept; contribute 0 revenue |
| Payment total differs from items + freight by > R$1 | 249 | GMV uses items + freight |

## 5. Limitations
- Olist is one marketplace, 2016-2018, Brazil. The numbers describe that business, not e-commerce in general.
- Correlation is not causation: late orders may also differ in product, region or seller.
  A controlled test (for example by carrier) would be needed to measure the causal effect.
- Reviews exist only for customers who chose to leave one.
